I've never been to church in my life, last time I was even in a church was fifteen years ago for a funeral.

I get that every one sits and some guy gives a sermon but apart from movies I know nothing about a typical Sunday for church goers.

What goes on before, during and after church?

That's going to depend on what church you're talking about. Most people show up on Sundays to listen to a sermon (basically selected parts of the Bible, possibly being related to current events). When they show up they're usually invited to greet their fellow parishioners and shake hands. Along with the sermon there is singing. Sometimes prayer requests are made. This is the beginning and end of things for mosh church goers.

I grew up attending a Methodist church. As a child I attended Sunday school while my parents attended the sermon. Upon arriving at church the children would generally be gathered to sing, then the class would start. Depending on the age group, that could be children playing games mixed with the teacher reading a bible based lesson and asking the children questions. Occasionally we would attend extra children's events or watch plays hosted at the church.

As an adult I found adult Bible studies to be the most worthwhile (these are generally held before the sermon). It's basically a group of people reading selected parts of the Bible (or possibly other books as well), and discussing the passages, current events, and sometimes personal experiences.

Pastors kid here; depends. Before church, you see people half dead, fake smiles, and kids that don't want to behave. People with coffee, sweets, and and trying to make it go bible class on time.

Some people will start getting the "sanctuary" ready. People who have to sing or play in the band leave bible class right away, instead of mingling, they'll do this afterwards.

The pastor will get into the office around 5 or 6 am to prepare for the sermon. The actual sermon will not start until 10 am. The pastor, depending on the church will set up the coffee, communion, and the sweets. During winter, the caretaker will shovel, salt, and walk through the church to unlock the classrooms, the offices, and the front doors. I bring this up, because there is not just one caretaker, each department will help the main caretaker. Help clean up after events, parties, even youth events.

The Youth Pastor, depending on location, will go around and pick up kids, and after church drop them off again. Done of the older (40-50's) will drive to get the, ... less moble, elderly people.

People visit, chat, catch up before and after. Sometimes there's a lunch at the church. More time to visit.

During the churchy part, you sit and are bored. You listen to old news and the new news that is coming up. You say hi to a few people with 3 meters of where you sit. You sing a few hymns or contemporary songs. Then, the pastor will give a 20 to 30 minute sermon. Here's where things will differ, I've been to a church that would last 4 hours, thats the sermon. Music there was for an hour before the pastor talked. And a half hour after the pastor talked. ..... I miss that place.

Although his brother John was well known as an antislavery congressman, Sherman did not oppose slavery and was sympathetic to Southerners' defense of the institution. Boyd of Virginia, an enthusiastic secessionist:

You people of the South don't know what you are doing. This country will be drenched in blood, and God only knows how it will end. It is all folly, madness, a crime against civilization! You people speak so lightly of war; you don't know what you're talking about. War is a terrible thing! You mistake, too, the people of the North. They are a peaceable people but an earnest people, and they will fight, too. They are not going to let this country be destroyed without a mighty effort to save it... Besides, where are your men and appliances of war to contend against them? The North can make a steam engine, locomotive, or railway car; hardly a yard of cloth or pair of shoes can you make. You are rushing into war with one of the most powerful, ingeniously mechanical, and determined people on Earth—right at your doors. You are bound to fail. Only in your spirit and determination are you prepared for war. In all else you are totally unprepared, with a bad cause to start with. At first you will make headway, but as your limited resources begin to fail, shut out from the markets of Europe as you will be, your cause will begin to wane. If your people will but stop and think, they must see in the end that you will surely fail.[30]
